rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for contrasting with what was just said, including sentence-final “though.”

example.english: I want to go, though it is raining today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 bat1 gwo3 gam1 jat6 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use 雖然 as the all-purpose concessive linker, especially when the following main clause does not explicitly begin with 但係.

example.english: Though it's raining today, I'm still going out.
example.traditional: 雖然今日落雨，我都照樣出街。
example.jyutping: seoi1 jin4 gam1 jat6 lok6 jyu5 ngo5 dou1 ziu3 joeng6 ceot1 gaai1

rows.jyutping: seoi1 jin4 A daan6 hai6 B
rows.note: Use this everyday pattern when you want to link an explicit although-clause to its contrasting main clause.

example.english: Though the road is far, we'll get there after walking for a while.
example.traditional: 雖然條路好遠，但係我哋行下行下就到喇。
example.jyutping: seoi1 jin4 tiu4 lou6 hou2 jyun5 daan6 hai6 ngo5 dei6 haang4 haa5 haang4 haa5 zau6 dou3 laa3

rows.note: Use this as a colloquial emphatic tag after a statement or question, especially for “Isn't it, though?”

example.english: This movie is really good, though, isn’t it?
example.jyutping: nei1 tou3 hei3 hou2 tai2 hai6 mai6 sin1

rows.note: Use this when the emphatic sense is “indeed” or “really,” rather than a rhetorical tag such as “係咪先.”

example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 dung3 wo3
